header.running_head: The Enthusiasm of the Sahabah (RA) to Die and Give their Lives in the path of Allaah

blocks.text: granted us victory. I then went to Hadhrat Nu'maan (RA) with a container of water. As I washed the sand from his face, he asked who I was. When I informed him that I was Ma'qal bin Yasaar, he asked, 'What has happened to the Muslims?' 'Allaah has given them victory,' I replied. He then said, 'All praise to Allaah! Write to Hadhrat Umar (RA) informing him of this.' It was then that his soul departed."[^1]

Hadhrat Jubayr (RA) has narrated the Battle of Nahaawind in detail. In his narration he quotes (the following words of Hadhrat Nu'maan (RA)), "Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ fought a battle and did not launch an attack at the beginning of the day, he did not rush until the time of (Zuhr) salaah had arrived, the winds started to blow and the battle could take place in a pleasant manner. It was this practice of Rasulullaah ﷺ that prevented me from attacking. (He then prayed) O Allaah! Bring comfort to my eyes today by granting such a victory to the Muslims that gives honour to Islaam and disgrace to the Kuffaar. Thereafter, grant me death as a martyr." He then address the Muslims saying, "Say 'Aameen', may Allaah bless you." The others then said "Aameen" and started to weep.[^2]
The Enthusiasm of the Sahabah (RA) to Die and Give their Lives in the path of Allaah
The Incident of Hadhrat Khaythama (RA) and his son

Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Bilaal narrates that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was leaving for the Battle of Badr, Hadhrat Sa'd bin Khaythama (RA) and his father Hadhrat Khaytama (RA) both decided to leave with Rasulullaah ﷺ. When Rasulullaah ﷺ heard about this, he instructed that only one of them should leave and (to decide who it would be) that they draw lots. It was then that Hadhrat Khaytama (RA) said to his son Sa'd (RA), "One of us will have to remain behind. Why don't you stay with the women?" Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) replied, "Had it not been to attain Jannah, I would have certainly given you preference (to have it your way). However, I really do aspire for martyrdom on this trip." When they drew lots, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA)'s name was drawn. He therefore left for Badr with Rasulullaah ﷺ where he was martyred by Amr bin Abd Wadd.[^3]
